notes: Chinese Government Scholarship (China Scholarship Council) - Type B for the Advanced Graduate Program, awarded through Peking University. This is a national/government scheme (CSC) with no programme-specific supervisor: applicants first gain admission to a self-funded full-time graduate programme of their own chosen major and are then nominated, so no professor is tied to the award. Official source: https://isd.pku.edu.cn/en/detail.php?id=819

Asian Future Leaders Scholarship Program (AFLSP) is a master's scholarship offered by the Bai Xian Asia Institute (BXAI) and administered through Tsinghua University. It is open to any full-time international master's programme; candidates are reviewed by the University's AFLSP Faculty Committee and recommended to BXAI. No named supervisor or programme faculty is tied to the award (it is a taught master's funding scheme, not research supervision). Official source: https://yz.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/info/1027/1477.htm ; sponsor: https://www.bxai.org/

notes: The Atomic Energy Scholarship Program of China is jointly initiated by the China Atomic Energy Authority (CAEA) and the Ministry of Education, with final assessment by the CAEA/MOE/CSC. It explicitly requires pre-admission to one of two Tsinghua departments: the Department of Engineering Physics (https://www.ep.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/) or the Institute of Nuclear and New Energy Technology (https://www.inet.tsinghua.edu.cn/ineten/), across nine nuclear research directions. The professors listed are INET faculty whose research areas match the scholarship's named directions, identified via INET's official Faculty pages; institutional emails were recorded only where published on the INET profile itself.
